questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of light is equal to $299{,}792{,}458 \text{ m s}^{-1}$
options: relative to a moving train on the earth.
only relative to the source of the light.
questions.solution:
According to the postulates of the special theory of relativity, the speed of light in vacuum is a universal constant.

It is independent of the relative motion of the source and the observer. Therefore, the speed of light is the same for all observers in inertial frames, regardless of their state of motion.

Thus, the speed of light is $299{,}792{,}458 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ relative to a moving train on the earth, relative to the sun, and relative to the earth.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following techniques can be employed to determine the speed of light in water?
questions.solution:
To determine the speed of light in a specific medium like water, we need a laboratory method where the required path length of light is relatively small, so that a tube filled with water can be placed in the optical path.

Roemer's method is an astronomical method based on the observation of the eclipses of Jupiter's moons, so it cannot be used to measure the speed of light in water.

Fizeau's method (using a toothed wheel) requires a very long path length (typically several kilometers). It is practically impossible to construct and maintain a water tube of such a large length.

Foucault's method uses a rotating mirror and requires a much shorter path length (a few meters). A tube filled with water can easily be placed between the rotating mirror and the fixed mirror to measure the speed of light in water. Foucault successfully used this to prove that light travels slower in water than in air.

Michelson's method is also a laboratory method (an improvement over Foucault's rotating mirror method) and can be similarly adapted to measure the speed of light in water by placing a water tube in the optical path.

Therefore, both Michelson's method and Foucault's method can be employed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following methods can be utilized to measure the speed of light inside a laboratory?
questions.solution:
Foucault's method uses a rotating mirror and a fixed concave mirror separated by a relatively small distance of a few meters. This compact setup allows the experiment to be performed inside a laboratory.

Fizeau's method requires a large distance of several kilometers between the source and the mirror.

Michelson's method uses a rotating octagonal mirror and requires a very large distance of tens of kilometers.

Roemer's method is an astronomical method based on the observation of the eclipses of Jupiter's moons.
